---
title: "A label that asks for its own window"
filters:
  - code-window
format:
  html: default
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
extensions:
  code-window:
    auto-filename: false
---

The document derives no names, yet the first block names its own label, so it
gets a window with that label. Each block after it writes something that wins
over the label, so none of them gets the label in its title bar.

```{.bash code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
echo forced
```

```{.bash filename="run.sh" code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
echo explicit
```

```{.bash code-window-enabled="false" code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
echo disabled
```

```{.bash code-window-no-auto-filename="true" code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
echo refused
```

A labelled block in a language Pandoc cannot highlight still goes through the
language pass, so it is framed like any other labelled block.

```{.foo code-window-auto-label="Shell"}
x = 1
```

A labelled block that turns the window off keeps the language its author wrote,
because no window reads the label.

```{.foo code-window-no-auto-filename="true" code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
x = 2
```

```{.foo code-window-enabled="false" code-window-auto-label="Terminal"}
x = 3
```
